Noah: flagging AuroraPay LoRA onboarding. Quickpack shows some negative amounts lose the minus sign after q4 quant. fp16 returns '-$12.34' but q4 returns '$12.34' (flip sign).

Priya: wow that's bad. any tokenizer weirdness with the minus/unicode minus?

Noah: we saw both ASCII '-' (U+002D) and Unicode '−' (U+2212) in source templates. quickpack used q4_0. Command: ./evalpack/run_quickpack.sh --model paynet-base-fp16 --adapter aurorapay-lora.safetensors --quant q4_0 --prompts tests/aurorapay/negatives.jsonl

Eli: can you paste a failing example?

Noah: Prompt: "Refund: −$12.34 -> Reason:" fp16 -> "−$12.34"; q4 -> "$12.34". Saved quickpack at s3://redwood-evals/aurorapay/quickpack/6799999999/

Priya: stopgap: normalize templates to ASCII '-' before serving. Also run token-diff to see if unicode minus maps to different token id under q4.

Noah: re-ran 30 examples with --save-tokens --save-logits. Uploaded tokens/logits to s3 path.

ci-bot: Adapter verification: aurorapay-lora passed signatures.

Eli: quick check: unicode minus tokenized as separate grapheme under q4, and quant logits for leading minus cluster drop below threshold, so decoder emits nothing for sign. Looks quant-noise related.

Priya: try two experiments: a) normalize minus to ASCII and re-run q4_0, b) merged-then-quant path. If merged path preserves sign, recommend merge for customer.

Noah: running both now. Will report results in thread.
